rationale: The strongest candidates are other short Eisenhower commendation letters, but their overlap with the Hogan telegram consists only of routine ceremonial language: congratulations, praise for distinguished service or achievement, patriotic framing, and best wishes. C14 is closest in combining a broad American constituency, commendation, personal gratitude, and best wishes; C17 shares congratulatory language and a “not only ... but also” praise construction; C01 pairs personal congratulations with “magnificent” performance. None contains sufficiently distinctive language, organization, or adapted administrative machinery to show that it materially supplied the Hogan telegram’s drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Millions of Americans would like to participate ... We are proud of you ... With best wishes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: patriotic Americans everywhere ... deserving of commendation ... Please accept my personal gratitude ... and my best wishes
shared_material.explanation: C14 has the closest ceremonial progression, but these are conventional elements of a presidential tribute.

shared_material.child_excerpt: not only as a great competitor ... but also as an envoy extraordinary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: not only fine soldiers but also statesmen ... to congratulate and salute them
shared_material.explanation: C17 shares a contrastive praise construction and congratulatory purpose, but the wording and structure are too generic to establish reuse.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: my personal congratulations on the magnificent performance
shared_material.explanation: C01 shares the pairing of congratulations with “magnificent,” but this isolated formula is ordinary congratulatory language.
